After finished reading a story the player is asked to answer some questions. These can be based on either reading skills or vocabulary building. There are different question formats: multiple choice or fill-in the blanks for reading questions and fill-in, synonyms or antonyms for vocabulary questions.

The program comes with an editor called myth maker that allows the user to create new stories as well as accompanying questions with answers. There is also a mythical match game which is a concentration game where the players have to flip cards to reveal pictures with the aim of uncovering all the images.

165355.overview: Mandragore is a role-playing game that was originally released in France. The kingdom was at peace under King Jorian. When he was killed in a freak accident that peace was shattered as Lord Yarod-Nor took control and began a reign of tyranny and evil. The player leads a party of four characters (with the option to either define your own characters or take a predefined group) through the land to eventually challenge, confront and defeat Yarod-Nor in his own castle. Before that can be done the group must explore nine chateaux each of which contains a problem and clues that are useful later in the game, battle assorted and unusual monsters, enter villages to trade, and develop your characters skills.

165569.overview:
Math Man is an educational arcade game for the Apple II.

Designed to teach basic math, there are 10 levels of increasing difficulty math problems. The player must move a character through a series of platforms and ladders containing tokens that either add or subtract numbers from an existing score on the top of the screen. The player's goal is to reach a specific number. They must accomplish this task before a bucket being hoisted on the right side of the screen reaches its zenith, and floods the entire maze, causing the player to lose a life. The player has a total of 3 lives, and each remaining life must finish the level to move onto the next. There are 4 levels of character movement speed available.

There is also an option to practice math without the arcade component.

165570.overview:
"Microzine" is an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 16 is a double-sided disk that features "Tickets to America" and "Solar Pilot."

The issue also containted "A Traveler's Guide to Fantastic Places," a database of real and fictional places.  Finally, "Shift Shapes" is a jigsaw type puzzle game.

165571.overview:
Microzine Jr is a disk magazine similar in format to the Microzine series.  It was targeted towards children grades 1 through 3.  

This issue contained the titles "Mask Maker", "Safari!", "Talk to B.E.R.T.," and "Eye Spy"

165580.overview: "Microzine" is an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992.  Issue 18 contains the titles "History Mystery", "LetterWriter", "ScholastiCalc", and "Rose & Calumny."

165633.overview:
Math Blaster Mystery is a junior high school level math and problem solving game for multiple systems.

There are 4 different math challenges, with each containing 4 levels of difficulty:

-    Decipher the Code - The player must decipher a mathematical equation by trying to fill in blanks. Each turn, every correct number or operation is kept for the next round. The goal is to decipher the algorithm in the minimal number of turns.
-    Follow the Steps - The player is walked through completing a word problem, by determining which information is important, how to solve the problem, and ultimately producing an answer
-    Search for Clues - The player searches an old house by selecting the items and people pictured. Each selection will give a clue to the mystery number. When the player has gathered enough evidence, they can solve the problem, with the goal being to use as few clues as possible.
-    Weigh the Evidence - A Tower of Hanoi based puzzle, where the goal is to place the desired weights on the scale to the far right.

165635.overview:
"Mr. and Mrs. Potato Head" is a 1985 educational game distributed by Random House, Inc.  

The box's back states:

"Generations of children have enjoyed creating their own Mr and Mrs Potato Head characters.  Now, for the first time, children can bring their creations to life!  On Side 1, players can choose to animate one ot he ready-made friendly, funny potato characters or choose to mix and match body parts to create their own unique potato fol.  SIde 2 contains Mr Potato Head and friends in three lively memory games deisgned to sharpen concentration and memory skills."

165660.overview:
Master of the Lamps casts you as an Eastern prince hoping to become King. There are two distinct gameplay sections, through which he must prove his worthiness. Firstly, you must ride a magic carpet, flying through a series of diamonds which twists and turns more as you move through the 41 levels. 

Alternating with this, you are in front of a row of pipes. Hit a gong 3 times to summon a genie, who will play a sequence of notes. Once the last one has been played, they fly towards you in order, and their colour equivalent on the row must be hit (the number of times they are played), before the flying note can hurt you. Complete this and a piece of lamp is granted.

165662.overview:
This issue of Microzine contains the following titles:

"Malice in Wonderland" is a math themed Twistaplot adventure.  "Animation Lab" is a simple and easy to use introduction to animation software.  "Calendar!" is a calendar tool.  "Estimator" is a math themed puzzle game.

165685.overview: "Microzine" is an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue 20 contains the titles "Voyage to See What's on the Bottom", "Interactionsr", Herioes and Villians", and "Monitor Mystery."

165702.overview: "Microzine" is an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue 21 from 1987 features "Robot Rescue", "Fill in the Blanks", "Fabulous Kids", and "Monitor Mystery"

165758.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 22 comes on two disks (one double-sided, one single-sided) and features "Haunted Channels", "NewsPrint.", "Math Mall", and "Monitor Mystery".

165761.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 23 features "Escape from ANTcatraz", "Monitor Mystery: The Case of the Foul Play", "Greetings", and "Math Mall"

165783.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 25 is a double-sided disk that features "Cosmic Heroes", "Blueprint Maker", "Picture This",  and "The Learning Machine."

165802.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 26 is a double-sided disk that features "The Wizard of Darkling Wood", "Congratulations!", "Picture This", and "Math Mall".

166276.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 27 features "Rebus Maker", "Constellation Odyssey", "The Learning Machine", and "Mystery on the High Seas!".

166309.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 28 features "Stationary Maker", "Quest for the Pole", "Sound Lab", and "African Animals".

166454.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 28 features "Screen Artistr", "The Myths of Olympus", "Light on Target", and "Desert Dilemma".

166556.overview: "Microzine" was an educational disk-based magazine published by Scholastic between 1983 and 1992. Issue no. 30 features "Poster Maker", "Toward the North Star", "Contraptions", and "Double Vision".

175319.overview: Issue 31 of Scholastic's Microzine series includes "Volcanic Voyager" a twistaplot adventure, which the editors describe as "explosive".  A puzzle adventure "Monitor Mystery" is also included, which asks the user to find a "mechanical mutt".  "Game Plan" is a limited game maker that has a focus on math.

175323.overview: Issue number 32 was the beginning of the end of Scholastic's long running successful edutainment series, Microzine.  This was the first issue to forgo the color software packaging with a generic cover.  That being said the software quality was just as high as ever.  This issue includes "Eyes on the World", "FYI: A Database", "A Night at Fleener's", and "The Case of the Unidentified Flying Alien."

175351.overview: Issue #33 of Scholastic's Microzine series includes another 4 programs including "Planet, Plan-It" which has the user create his own solar system.  Other programs include "Historical Hysterics", "Word War", and "Going to Pieces"

175352.overview: In Microzine issue #34, "The Case of the Missing Rose" is a mystery adventure which has the player assuming the role of Ed Minkly searching for the whereabouts of the white rose.  "Secret Sentences" is a word guessing game similar to hang-man.  "The Mystery of the Olympic Impostors" asks the player to investigate the disappearance of 3 olympic athletes with a 1 hour time limit.  Finally, "FYI: A Database of Inventions" is a database of over 100 inventions.

175353.overview: Microzine issue #35 includes "Grid Block" is a puzzlewhich requires the user to unscramble blocks.  "What's Missing" is another puzzle game where the user pieces together puzzles.  "World Agent" asks the user to look for a stolen national treasure from Washington DC.  "Let's Graph It" is a simple graphing program

175362.overview: Issue # 36 of Scholastic's Microzine series has another 4 programs for grade school children.  The first title, "The Case of the Crafty Caper," is a mystery adventure.  The second program, "Trap Doors," is a puzzle game that has the player avoiding trap doors in a spooky old house.  The third title, "Dr Think and the Idea Factory," has the player explore the thoughts of past inventors.  The final title, "It Fits!," is a puzzle game.

175374.overview:
Microzine issue number 37 contains 4 programs: The Case of the Cutting Caper, Math Mall, The Race for Independence, and Nutrition Explorer.

From the Letter from the Editor:

What's new in Microzine? Lots! We guarantee you'll have fun playing with this issue.  And don't tell anyone, but you'll probably learn something too!  Look at PROGRAMS on the Guide to see what each program is all about.

"Nutrition Explorer" lets you examine the foods you eat.  Do you think you eat a well balanced diet?

175591.overview: Microzine 38 includes another four programs. "Eskimo Escapade" is a puzzle game that has the player searching pictures for anomalies and identifying them.  "Math Mall" is a math game involving fractions and decimals.  "Out Space Adventures in Government" is an educational adventure game that has the player travelling the solar system when the player's ship crashes. Finally. "Exploring Simple Machines" has the player creating simple machines to solve simple tasks

175832.overview: Meme les Pommes de Terre Ont des Yeux is a text adventure game released by Froggy Software in 1985 for Apple II . The game is characterized by a tone of humor (black in particular). Like almost all Froggy games, the illustration of the jacket is signed by Jean Solé .

176240.overview:
This language skills educational game allows you to create original crossword puzzles using word clues or 185 illustrations, which can be used as picture clues. After entering the clues, you can randomly generate puzzles that you can solve yourself or play against Mickey (hard), Donald (medium) or Goofy (easy). The game features bonus and super bonus points, more than 20 musical tunes and a fireworks display for the winner. You can also print your creations using Disney backgrounds or borders, including such characters as Dumbo, Peter Pan, Snow White and many more. Picture menu bars guides you through both the game and the tools for creating and printing out puzzles.

The Apple II version is one of the last few commercial releases

176244.overview:
Mind Pursuit is a trivia game where one to four players try to answer questions in a variety of subjects in three different game modes. The three game modes have you trying to win the game by answering questions either to a certain amount of points, get as many points within a time limit or play on a board. You press the space to throw a dice and the number corresponds to a subject which are Science & Nature, History & Geography, TV & Movies, Sport & Games, Culture or Grab Bag. There are three type of questions to choose from, Fill in the Blanks which is worth 100 points, Multiple Choice which is worth 50 points, or True or False which is worth 25 points. Get a question correct and the player gets another question but get it wrong and the next player gets a question.

For point limit you have the choice of 500, 1000, 1500 or 200 points and you can select the time to answer a question, 30 seconds, 45 seconds, 60 seconds or no time limit. For time limit you have the choice of 30 minutes, 60 minutes, 90 minutes or 120 minutes, and you can select the length of answering a question. These modes are text only but the occasional question has music or sounds.

The board game itself allows you the length of answering a question and you can choose a character as a piece. The board itself is an isometric view with the whole board shown on the screen. The players start in the bottom left and have to make it to the top left of the screen. There are various squares and each have 100, 50 or 25 on them. Once again you throw the dice to get a subject for a question and you move to the next square. 25 and 50 squares allow you the choice of question type but a 100 square only allows you to answer a Fill in the Blanks question. Getting a question correct and you move the amount dictated by the amount of the square you were on.

205629.overview:
Mutant is a 1-player arcade game for the Apple II.

The player controls a small spaceship which can move horizontally on the bottom of the screen, and fire vertically forwards. Numerous waves of mutants appear on the screen, and the player must repeatedly shoot each monster to destroy it. As he monsters are shot, they change into different creatures, until eventually being destroyed after multiple hits. Enemies can enter from all 4 sides of the screen, including from directly behind or beside the player. The player has 3 lives, and when all are lost, it's game over.

219597.overview: Match Wits is a memory/concentration game mixed with elements from quiz and word guessing games. The game is for two players who take turns turning over squares to reveal the hidden words. The aim is to pick pairs of matching words which are then removed from the board. As squares are removed a hidden picture puzzle begins to be revealed and the players get chances to guess on its meaning. The player that enters the correct answer will win the round. A game consists of three rounds and the player with the highest score wins. There are six different subject categories to choose from: animals, cities, multiplication, words, sports and famous people. The game also comes with a secretary program that allows the player to edit and add content to the game.

421489.overview: Mind Castle I is an educational title that teaches logic and reasoning. You begin by entering the basement of a mysterious, seemingly abandoned castle. There you are greeted by Mr. Winn, who says that a treasure awaits you at the top of a tower, but you must first solve puzzles and riddles to move up the floors of the castle. The puzzles themselves are generally of the type that require recognizing patterns. They can also be logic puzzles where you deduce who is lying based on statements made. They may also be a simple play on words. Mr. Winn can offer hints, but it is up to you to solve the puzzles of each floor to make it to the top of the tower.

421494.overview: The earliest commercial home computer port of the first mainframe adventure game, Colossal Cave. Players explore said cave, searching for treasure, solving puzzles, using magic, avoiding threatening little dwarves, and navigating mazes of twisty passages, all alike.

422200.overview: As the adventurer Brian Hammerhand you have to defeat the Wizard Morloc the Mad in his Tower. The towers stairways comprise Rooms 1-6. With the exception of the ground floor, which has been assigned the next several room numbers, rooms with odd numbers are on Floors 1, 3, and 5, and rooms with even numbers are on Floors 2, 4, and 6. The higher the number, the higher the floor on which the room is located. While your journey you meet many bad creatures and you will find some magic and helpful treasures.

423204.overview:
Utilizing a birds-eye view of the golf course, the player chooses their club and the direction of their shot. The player chooses shot direction by positioning the golfer's feet around the ball. The player also choose from 5 different strengths of shot (light, fair, medium, firm, and strong), and how much curve they wish to apply. Wind and terrain play a role in game play, and players must avoid sand and water traps.

When the player lands a ball on the green, game play shifts to a zoomed in birds-eye view of the green. The player must then carefully play their putting to place the ball within the hole. Score is maintained through all 18 holes.

The game also comes with a scenario editor, which allows the player to make and store custom holes to distribute to other players.

423233.overview:
Megabots is a futuristic strategy game that utilizes 3D graphics, animation, music and sound effects.

The game begins with an introduction to set the scene before the player enters a grid filled with robots that might be good or bad. The objective to find a power cell within the grid to move on to the next level. Good robots can be interrogated for information. Bad robots must be destroyed with the right weapon before you can move past them. The strategy element comes from choosing the right weapons for the bad robots, and navigating the grid based on the information received to find the power cell before the player's own power reserve is depleted.

423290.overview:
Just when you thought it was safe to go back into the mine. The sequel to the original Miner 2049er, it contains 10 more levels of difficult futuristic mines to explore.

You play the part of Bounty Bob, and it is your mission to explore every inch of an abandoned mine. As you walk over floor sections in the mine, the floor will change color. When all of the floor sections have been changed in color, you can move on to the next, more challenging level. Yukon Yohan has a whole bag of dirty tricks to prevent you from thoroughly exploring each level.

You can jump (be careful not to fall too far though, or you will be squished), climb up and down ladders, and use different transportation devices that can be found on the levels. You'll encounter ricocheting ore jumps, time warp transporters, and radioactive stalactites. Wandering around the mine are numerous radioactive creatures which get in Bounty Bob's way. Also scattered throughout the mines are various artifacts left behind; if Bounty Bob collects one of these, the creatures will temporarily become vulnerable. If Bounty Bob runs into one of the creatures in this state the creature will be destroyed, but if he runs into a creature while it is glowing Bounty Bob will be destroyed.

423291.overview:
Might & Magic: The Lava Pits of Aznar is a text-based adventure game with RPG elements.

Create a character and travel the dark worlds on Wingster in search of treasure and power. Journey into the Lava Pits of Aznar in search of the amulet of the High Lord. Designed as an adventure game with roleplaying elements, the player at the beginning of each game chooses from either Wizard, Warrior, or Thief, and from 4 different races. Statistics are modified on character creation. The player must explore the underground via basic text VERB NOUN commands, but also must navigate combat against the denizens of the lava pits. Characters must eat and sleep during their adventure, and their statistics will be reduced if they do not remain healthy.

423345.overview: Mychess II Is an early chess game for multiple platforms, and the sequel to Mychess. Games can be played 2-player or versus the computer. Players must type in their individual move commands, and only legitimate moves are allowed. Players can set up individual chess challenges, replay famous games from history, and can set time limits between moves for tournament play. Gameplay can be displayed in text-only mode, in a traditional 2D view, or in 3D mode.

423839.overview: Mystery Fun House is the seventh entry in the original Scott Adams adventure series. The events of the game take place at an amusement park. The first puzzle involves figuring out how to get in past the turnstiles. Once inside, the player must solve the mystery of the place, going through a house of mirrors and so forth. Like the others in the series, the game is a text adventure with a rather basic two-word command parser. The Japanese computer versions feature graphics in addition to the text input.

424013.overview:
An extremely hard to find game. It is a fantasy adventure where you can create your own characters, choose from a wide inventory of weapons and armor, and use freeform input combined with making choices to explore a dungeon. Watch out for the Chromatic Dragon!

This is a dungeon crawl game - equip your character, enter the dungeon, fight monsters and win treasure; traps abound as well. Many events are random. You can save your character (assuming he survives) to use in later episodes.

Balrog was a 'sampler' of the Maces and Magic series, with only the later ones being full games.

424163.overview: Compose and play a musical score using an easy graphical interface and toolkit. Use a pointer to drag notes, sharps, and other music nomenclature directly onto a staff, then play your creation. You can cut, copy, and paste entire sections of music, as well as print your masterpiece.

448015.overview:
During the player's adventures in Mind Castle I, they escaped the haunted old mansion owned by Mr. Winn.

Upon visiting their local library, the player finds an old newspaper clippings about millions in old Confederate bills that may be hidden deep within the deceased Mr. Winn's mansion. The old mansion out on Route 1 has now been boarded up for public safety, but the desire for adventure and riches gets the better of the player, and they decide to investigate the building. Upon climbing through a gate to the basement, the player becomes trapped within Mind Castle.

Here, the player meets a number of Mr. Winn's family and employees, who still possess the mansion. The player must move between rooms of the mansion, while they slowly work their way up a number of floors. Each room possesses a riddle based upon logic or pattern recognition. If the player completes enough riddles, they move to a higher floor, where they meet a new riddlemaster. The residents of the manor can offer hints if requested. The challenges become more difficult as the player ascends.

448063.overview: In Release 2 of Millionaire: The Stock Market Simulation, where margin and short sales are added to gameplay, you are starting a session at U.S. stock market with Net Worth equal to $10,000. Three companies from Automobile, Computer, Oil & Gas, Aerospace, and Food Industries are present on this market. Stock prices are changing each week due to economical, political, or social situation. You should in turns examine the news and trends, and buy or sell a certain quantity of stocks, increasing your Net Worth. Based on Net Worth, you'll be classified by one of the five ranks: Novice, Investor, Speculator, Professional, or Broker. The higher rank you have, more Investment Opportunities you use. The goal is to finish the session with as greater Net Worth as possible, but you should remember that the highest rank is Millionaire. The game is available for one or several players. Each session is saved in progress and may be restored later. A number of adjustments such as different rates (Loan interest, Cash interest, Commission, Tax) or visuals may be adjusted.

448938.overview: Microgammon is a computer adaptation of the Backgammon board game for one person playing against an AI opponent. The game uses simple text based graphics to draw the board as well as the dice. The game is played with the keyboard. Each point on the board has a number and to make a move the player simply types in the number of the starting point followed by the end point.

449055.overview:
Merlin's Castle is a graphical text adventure.

The player must infiltrate Merlin's Castle in search of treasure while avoiding dangers. All commands are via VERB NOUN entries, and the player must solve several inventory-based puzzles. There is no save/restore feature.

450045.overview:
Microscopic Journey is a 1-player arcade game for the Apple II.

The player controls a small ship that has been shrunk to fit within a human blood vessel. The player must race against time to reach specific human organs to target disease within these areas. While in a blood vessel, the player can move up and down, but can also accelerate forwards. The ship is armed with a small laser which can shoot platelets and white blood cells that attempt to impede travel. If the player goes off course and pierces the edge of a blood vessel, the vessel must be repaired. Damaging a major vessel 3 times can cause sufficient blood loss to kill the host. Platelets will stick to the player and slow them down, preventing the player from reaching their target organ in time. If a white blood cell attaches to the player, their ship will be dissolved if the cell is not lost by crashing through the vessel wall.

457063.overview: Music theory training games for children.

457072.overview:
Designed to teach children age 6 - 10 basic spelling and grammar rules, it consists of a series of three mini-games with animated graphics and sound. In each section, the player can choose words from a number of categories, including: animals, orchestra, fruit, and more.

Scramble Spells - The player is given a list of words, and the letters have been scrambled. The player must correctly unscramble each word.

Flash Spells - Words are displayed on the screen for a few seconds, and the player must memorize their spelling and correctly type them.

Players can create and modify their own set of words, and copy them to another disk to allow other players to participate.

457203.overview:
An alien mother ship approaches on your screen, hovering high above the Earth. As you grab the lever of your assault vessel, the mother ship begins to fill attack raiders into the chutes, ready to rain destruction upon the planet's surface. Once the chutes are filled, raiders begin to descend, intent upon your destruction.

In Mission: Invasion Force, the player controls a small space vessel on the bottom of the screen, which can scroll left and right, while firing shots vertically. Above the player, an endless array of small vessels descend from the chutes above, and the player gains points by destroying as many vessels as possible, while a timer counts down from 250. Intermittently, larger bonus vessels will descend from the center of the screen or the peripheries. If the player comes in contact with a descending vessel, their ship is destroyed. The player has a total of 5 vessels, and when all are lost, it's game over.

460372.overview:
Murder on the Atlantic takes place on the Bourgogne, a big French ocean liner, in 1938. On board: various rich people along with spies which want to snare the new computer technology for their own needs. The player takes the role of a detective who has to solve two mysterious murders which took place on the Bourgogne.

The game is completely menu driven. The player chooses which part of the ship he wants to go next. Here he can examine the room or interrogate one of the 40 suspects. The player does not directly interact with the suspects, he only gets to read their statement. During the course of the game he also finds a decoder which can be used to decrypt messages. Puzzles consist of finding code words.

This part has no defined ending. When the player has puzzled together the solution - he also needs to use the many documents which are delivered with the game in physical form - he starts the second part of the game. Here he needs to answer a series of questions and, if they are correct, he wins.

460381.overview: Micro Barmate is your computer age bar guide for parties and entertainment.

460389.overview:
Mind Prober asks users questions to rate themselves or other people on a series of 23 adjectives (talkative, pleasure-seeking, etc.), computes the results, and prints a three-page report describing the person.

The questions for users differ by gender (male or female) and age (under 18, or 18 and older). The program comes with a thick manual-plus-book that contains many chapters on how to better understand people around you.

461496.overview: Mimic is a Simon Says style game. Nine tiles displayed in a grid on the screen will light up and the player must repeat the sequence. The sequence will get longer and longer until the player makes a mistake.

464130.overview:
Max-Command is a strategy war-game for the Apple II.

For the past several months, high level negotiations and diplomatic talks have continued in order to avoid a serious confrontation between two nations. World intelligence sources report that both countries have just broken off diplomatic ties. Increased military buildup near the plains of Alphagorda has now escalated to open conflict and a state of war now exists between the two powers.

A 1-player versus computer or 2-player strategy war game, the player takes control of one nation's military forces in a square grid of randomly placed forests, mountains, lakes, and swamps. Units consist of planes, tank corps, mobile laser artillery, armored infantry, missile batteries, and "The Max-One". Each unit has their own movement radius, firing distance, and terrain allowances. Random weather changes will modify the mobility and firing radius of units every few turns.

Players are awarded points for enemy units destroyed, and games can proceed until a certain score is reached, or until all enemy units are terminated.
